transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported Rust mutable slice pattern `if let [.., last] = self { Some(last) } else { None }` to the reviewed mutable split-last desugaring: `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at_mut(slice.len() - 1)`, and `&mut tail[0]`.

Added proof-only split_at_mut view assertions and a sequence-update equality connecting the returned mutable last element to the exact-vstd final-frame postcondition; these annotations do not change executable control flow or data flow.
